quiz.title: T5.3: Common Runtime Errors
quiz.description: Diagnose and fix common ObjectScript runtime errors: <SUBSCRIPT>, <PROTECT>, <FRAMESTACK>, <UNDEFINED>, and related errors

questions.question:
A background task running using the BackgroundDev role calls:

zn "STORE-BASE"
set obj = ##class(Sample.Customer).%OpenId(123)
set obj.City = "Ulaanbaatar"
set sc = obj.%Save()

The code terminates with a <PROTECT> error:

ZN "STORE-BASE"
^
 */db/iris/mgr/STOREBASE-DATA/

Which explanation best describes why?
options: The global backing Sample.Customer resides in a database mounted read-only
The current user holds no UPDATE privilege on table Sample.Customer via SQL grants
Another process has a LOCK on the specific row, causing a lock conflict
The value "Ulaanbaatar" exceeds the defined column length
BackgroundDev does not have permission to access the database underpinning the STORE-BASE namespace
questions.explanation: The <PROTECT> error with the database path shown indicates a security protection violation at the database level. The BackgroundDev role lacks the required resource permission (Read/Write) on the STOREBASE-DATA database. SQL UPDATE privileges are separate from database-level resource permissions. Lock conflicts produce <LOCKTAB>, not <PROTECT>. This matches InterSystems practice question Q23. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

options: Line 4 uses a variable (ordKey) that was never set -- the developer likely meant to use 'key'
Line 3 contains invalid syntax for the quit command
$ORDER sets ordKey to an empty string which cannot be used as a subscript
Line 3 improperly contains two commands on one line
questions.explanation: The variable 'ordKey' on line 4 was never assigned a value anywhere in the method. The developer most likely meant to write 'key' (which is set by $ORDER on line 3) instead of 'ordKey'. The <UNDEFINED> error with *ordKey confirms the exact variable that is undefined. The postconditional quit:key="" syntax on line 3 is valid ObjectScript. This matches InterSystems practice question Q24. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
A developer runs the following code and gets a <SUBSCRIPT> error:

Set data(1) = "Alpha"
Set data(2) = "Beta"
Set data(3) = "Gamma"
Set key = ""
For {
    Set key = $Order(data(key))
    Quit:key=""
    Write data(key), !
}

Another developer modifies it to:

Set key = ""
For {
    Set key = $Order(data(key))
    Write data(key), !
    Quit:key=""
}

The modified version produces a <SUBSCRIPT> error. Why?
options: $Order does not work with local arrays, only globals
The Quit:key="" check moved AFTER Write data(key), so when $Order returns "" at the end, data("") is accessed before the loop exits
The For loop syntax is invalid without start:step:end
data(key) requires a numeric subscript, and $Order returns strings
questions.explanation: In the modified code, when $Order returns "" after the last node, the Write data("") executes BEFORE the Quit:key="" check. Accessing data("") with an empty string subscript produces a <SUBSCRIPT> error. The original code correctly places Quit:key="" before the Write, so the loop exits before attempting to read data(""). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

options: Change 'return' to 'quit'
Add a base case: If n <= 1 { return 1 }
Use a larger stack size with $SYSTEM.Process.SetStackSize()
Replace recursion with: set result = n!
questions.explanation: The method recurses infinitely because there is no base case to stop the recursion. When n reaches 0, it continues with -1, -2, etc., never stopping. Adding 'If n <= 1 { return 1 }' at the beginning provides the stopping condition that prevents infinite recursion and the resulting <FRAMESTACK> error. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
What error does this code produce?

Set name = "John"
Set age = 30
Write "Name: " _ name _ ", Age: " _ agee
options: <SYNTAX> because of the concatenation operator
<UNDEFINED> *agee because 'agee' is a typo for 'age'
<ILLEGAL VALUE> because you cannot concatenate strings and numbers
No error -- 'agee' evaluates to empty string
questions.explanation: The variable 'agee' (with double 'e') was never defined. ObjectScript variable names are case-sensitive and must match exactly, so 'agee' is a different variable from 'age'. This is one of the most common causes of <UNDEFINED> errors: simple typos in variable names. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
A developer sees this error in production:

<UNDEFINED> zProcess+15^App.Engine.1 *config

What does this error message tell us?
options: The class App.Engine does not exist
The variable 'config' was not defined at line offset 15 in the zProcess label of App.Engine.1
The process with PID 15 crashed in App.Engine
The global ^config is not defined in the current namespace
questions.explanation: The error format is: <ErrorType> label+offset^routine *variablename. So <UNDEFINED> zProcess+15^App.Engine.1 *config means the variable 'config' was undefined at offset 15 from the label zProcess in the compiled routine App.Engine.1. The asterisk (*) prefix indicates the specific undefined variable. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question: Which of the following can cause a <PROTECT> error? (Select three)
options: Writing to a database that is mounted read-only
Accessing a namespace without the required role/resource permission
Trying to modify a global node that another process has locked
The user's roles lack Write permission on the database resource
Using SET on a variable that already has a value
questions.explanation: <PROTECT> errors are security-related: (1) writing to a read-only database, (2) accessing a namespace/database without the required security role, (3) the user's roles lacking Write permission on the database resource. Lock conflicts produce <LOCKTAB>, not <PROTECT>. SET on an existing variable simply overwrites it. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
A developer wants to prevent <UNDEFINED> errors when accessing a variable that might not be set. Which approach is correct?

Option A: If $Data(timeout) { Set val = timeout }
Option B: Set val = $Get(timeout, 30)
Option C: Set val = $Find(timeout)
Option D: Set val = $Length(timeout)
options: Only option A works -- $Data checks if a variable is defined
Option B is the most direct approach -- $Get returns the default value if undefined
Option C -- $Find safely returns the variable's value
Both $Data and $Length work equally well
questions.explanation: $Get(variable, default) returns the value of the variable if defined, or the specified default if undefined, all without raising an <UNDEFINED> error. In option B, if 'timeout' is not defined, $Get returns 30. While $Data (option A) also works, it requires an extra If statement. $Find and $Length would themselves cause <UNDEFINED> if the variable is not set. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fget)

options: <UNDEFINED> on iteration 3 because $List returns undefined for null elements
No error — null is treated as 0 in arithmetic
<NULL VALUE> on iteration 3 because $List on a null list element raises this error
<SUBSCRIPT> on iteration 3 because the list element is null
questions.explanation: In $ListBuild, a missing element (double comma: $LB(10,20,,40)) creates a null entry — distinct from an empty string "". Calling $List() on a null element raises a <NULL VALUE> error. This is a common trap: $LB(10,20,"",40) with an explicit empty string would NOT error ("" coerces to 0 in arithmetic), but $LB(10,20,,40) with a null element does. Use $ListGet(list, i, default) instead of $List() to safely handle null elements. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
Consider this code:

ClassMethod BuildTree(node, depth)
{
    Set ^Tree(node) = depth
    Do ..BuildTree(node _ ".L", depth + 1)
    Do ..BuildTree(node _ ".R", depth + 1)
}

What error will occur first and why?
options: <SUBSCRIPT> because the node subscript eventually exceeds the maximum key length (511 bytes)
<FRAMESTACK> because there is no base case to stop the recursion
<MAXSTRING> because the node string concatenation exceeds the maximum string length
<STORE> because the ^Tree global fills the database
questions.explanation: Although there is no base case (which would eventually cause <FRAMESTACK>), the <SUBSCRIPT> error occurs first IN THIS CODE. Each recursive call appends 2 characters (".L" or ".R") to the node string used as a global subscript, and the maximum global reference length is 511 bytes - reached after roughly 250 levels. The call-stack limit is thousands of frames deep, so it is nowhere near exhausted by then: <SUBSCRIPT> occurs after 251 entries with a 501-character key. This ordering is not a general rule about the two errors - it follows from this code growing the subscript on every call. Unbounded recursion that does NOT build a longer global reference each time (a method that simply calls itself, say) never approaches the subscript limit and does terminate with <FRAMESTACK>. Whichever limit the code reaches first is the error you get. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RERR_gen)

questions.question: Which of the following can cause a <SUBSCRIPT> error? (Select two)
options: Setting a global node with an empty string subscript: Set ^Data("") = 1
Using $Order with an empty string starting value: Set key = $Order(^Data(""))
Using a subscript that exceeds the maximum key length (511 bytes)
Using a negative number as a subscript: Set ^Data(-5) = 1
Using a subscript longer than 31 characters
questions.explanation: <SUBSCRIPT> means the subscript itself was invalid: an empty string subscript in a SET, or a key that pushes past the maximum length. $ORDER(^Data("")) is legal and is in fact the standard way to start an iteration, and negative numbers are perfectly valid subscripts. The 31-character figure is invented -- the real constraint is the total key length (511 bytes), not a per-subscript character count.

questions.question:
A developer tries to write to a global in the IRISSYS database:

Set ^["IRISSYS"]MyGlobal("key") = "value"

This produces a <PROTECT> error. What is the most likely reason?
options: The extended global reference syntax ^["namespace"]global is incorrect
IRISSYS is a system database and the application user lacks Write permission on it
Global names stored in IRISSYS must start with %
The ^[] syntax requires three parameters: namespace, directory, and global name
questions.explanation: The IRISSYS database contains system data and is protected. Application users typically do not have Write permission to IRISSYS -- only users with %All or specific system administration roles can write to it. This is a database-level <PROTECT> error. The extended global reference syntax is correct. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
A developer writes:

ClassMethod ProcessFile(filename As %String) As %Status
{
    Set stream = ##class(%Stream.FileCharacter).%New()
    Set sc = stream.LinkToFile(filename)
    While 'stream.AtEnd {
        Set line = stream.ReadLine()
        Set parts = $Length(line, ",")
        Set orderId = $Piece(line, ",", 1)
        Set total = total + $Piece(line, ",", 3)
    }
    Write "Grand total: ", total, !
    Quit $$$OK
}

On the first iteration, the method fails with <UNDEFINED> *total. What is the fix?
options: Declare total as a parameter: ClassMethod ProcessFile(filename, total = 0)
Add 'Set total = 0' before the While loop
Change the + operator to _ (concatenation) which handles undefined variables
Use 'New total' before the loop to initialize it
questions.explanation: The variable 'total' is used in the expression 'total + $Piece(line, ",", 3)' before it has been assigned any value. On the first iteration, 'total' is undefined, causing <UNDEFINED>. The fix is to initialize it: 'Set total = 0' before the While loop. The 'New' command creates a new scope for a variable but does not assign it a value. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
A developer writes code that processes patient records:

ClassMethod UpdatePatients() As %Status
{
    Set key = ""
    For {
        Set key = $Order(^Patient(key))
        Quit:key=""
        Set name = ^Patient(key, "Name")
        Set city = ^Patient(key, "City")
        Set ^Report(name, City) = key
    }
    Quit $$$OK
}

The method produces: <UNDEFINED> *City
Which line has the bug?
options: The $Order line -- it should use $Order(^Patient(key), 1, data)
The 'Set ^Report(name, City)' line -- 'City' (capital C) is a different variable than 'city' (lowercase c)
The 'Set city' line -- ^Patient(key, "City") does not exist for some records
The For loop is missing start:step:end arguments
questions.explanation: ObjectScript variables are case-sensitive. The code sets 'city' (lowercase c) but references 'City' (capital C) in the ^Report subscript. These are two different variables, and 'City' was never assigned. The fix is to use consistent casing: Set ^Report(name, city) = key. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question: Which of the following runtime errors are correctly matched with their descriptions? (Select two)
options: <SUBSCRIPT> -- an invalid subscript value was used in a global or local array reference
<PROTECT> -- a memory protection fault occurred in the operating system kernel
<FRAMESTACK> -- the call stack exceeded its maximum depth, usually from infinite recursion
<UNDEFINED> -- a class definition could not be found in the database
<STORE> -- the database ran out of disk space while writing a global
questions.explanation: <SUBSCRIPT> is an invalid subscript in a global or local reference, and <FRAMESTACK> is the call stack exceeding its depth, usually through runaway recursion. <PROTECT> is a database PROTECTION error -- access denied to a global or database -- not an OS kernel fault, and <UNDEFINED> is a reference to an unset variable or global node, nothing to do with missing classes (that is <CLASS DOES NOT EXIST>). <STORE> is likewise about memory, not disk: the process exhausted its partition, which is why it is fixed by raising the process memory limit rather than by freeing disk.

options: <DIVIDE> because scores is 0 (no arguments) and the final line divides by zero
<UNDEFINED> *scores because the variadic array is not defined with zero arguments
<FUNCTION> because the ... syntax is invalid in ObjectScript
<PARAMETER> because at least one argument is required for variadic methods
questions.explanation: When a variadic method (scores...) is called with no arguments, the 'scores' variable is NOT set at all — it is undefined. The very first reference to 'scores' in the For loop (For i = 1:1:scores) produces an <UNDEFINED> *scores error. The variable is not automatically initialized to 0. The fix is to check '$GET(scores, 0)' or '$DATA(scores)' before using it. When called with arguments, 'scores' is set to the argument count and scores(1), scores(2), etc. hold the values. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GOBJ_methods)

options: <FRAMESTACK> because of infinite recursion
No error terminates the code, but it runs in an infinite loop because the While condition is never false
<SUBSCRIPT> because the subscripts cycle repeatedly
<UNDEFINED> because ^LinkedList eventually references a non-existent node
questions.explanation: This is not recursive (no method calls itself), so <FRAMESTACK> does not apply. The While loop follows the "Next" pointers endlessly since the circular reference means current never becomes "". The code runs in an infinite loop. The fix is to track visited nodes or set a maximum iteration count. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)

questions.question:
A method receives an object reference and processes it:

ClassMethod ProcessOrder(order As App.Order) As %Status
{
    Set customerId = order.CustomerId
    Set customer = ##class(App.Customer).%OpenId(customerId)
    Set email = customer.Email
    Do ..SendConfirmation(email, order.OrderNumber)
    Quit $$$OK
}

If customerId is valid but the customer record was deleted between the time the order was created and now, which error occurs on the third line?
options: <UNDEFINED> *customer because %OpenId returns "" for a deleted record
<INVALID OREF> because customer is "" (not an object) and .Email is called on it
<PROTECT> because the customer record is locked by the deletion process
<SUBSCRIPT> because the customer ID subscript no longer exists in the global
questions.explanation: When %OpenId cannot find the record (because it was deleted), it returns an empty string "". The next line attempts customer.Email on this empty string, which is not a valid object reference, producing <INVALID OREF>. The safe pattern is: Set customer = ##class(App.Customer).%OpenId(customerId)  If customer = "" { Quit $$$ERROR(...) }. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_errors)
